name: farkle-r1
context:
GAME ONE OF THREE, PUT TO YOU BEFORE ANY OF IT IS BUILT. Fifty-two proposed changes to finish a Farkle-on-a-grid game. Nothing below is implemented.

─────────── WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, READ NOT RECALLED ───────────

I read libriopal/magentadice-cyancode at commit 8db018e. Its farkle-engine is four small files and it is genuinely good:

  farkleScorer.ts  scoreFarkle(faces, multiplier) -> {score, scaledScore, isFarkle, combo, triggersBomb}. Marked SACRED, 16/16 tests, and its header records WHY: an earlier greedy scorer returned 1200 for two triplets [1,1,1,2,2,2] where exhaustive returns 2500.
  chainIndex.ts    encodes up to six dice into a dense base-6 integer, (length-1)*46656 + base6, and PRECOMPUTES all 279,936 scores into an Int32Array once. Scoring is then an array read.
  csprng.ts        HMAC-SHA256 keyed on (seed, counter). Commit-reveal with constant-time compare.
  types.ts         DieFace = 1..6.

Our repo has: a 6x6 board with pip tokens drawn through a 4D projection (engine/math/rotor4.ts, web/board4d.ts); a generic Ruleset<C,A> contract the server verifies by REPLAYING rather than re-implementing (net/heat-server.ts); pari-mutuel settlement (matchpoints x2 -> Neuberg -> pool closure); and a two-row forecast strip whose row 1 is certain and row 2 fallible (lattice/draw-stream.ts).

─────────── THE CORE LOOP I AM PROPOSING ───────────

Farkle scoring is about a HAND — a multiset of up to six dice. A match-3 grid is about ADJACENCY. The game is the join: the player traces a connected chain of up to six cells on the 6x6 grid, and the faces under that chain are scored as a Farkle hand.

That makes it structurally different from our other two modes in a way I can state precisely:
  lattice  bank ONE cell; the skill is inferring a hidden graph.
  chem     select a region; the skill is knowing what molecules exist.
  farkle   trace a PATH of up to six; the skill is reading combinations against a pay table you can memorise.

─────────── 52 PROPOSED CHANGES ───────────

RULES AND SCORING (1-12)
1 Chain length capped at 6, matching the die-hand size the scorer was built for. 2 The chain must be orthogonally connected, no diagonals, no revisits. 3 Score comes ONLY from lookupScore against the precomputed table — never a second scoring path. 4 A chain scoring 0 is a FARKLE and costs the turn. 5 Farkling is the risk that makes the push-your-luck real; without a loss condition a chain-tracer just always takes the biggest. 6 HOT DICE: clearing a chain that uses all six cells of a region refills and lets the player continue the same turn. 7 Banking is explicit — the player chooses to stop, exactly as in tabletop Farkle. 8 Unbanked score is lost on a farkle. 9 The pay table is PUBLISHED in the rules screen, because a memorisable table is the skill and hiding it makes it a slot machine. 10 Two triplets = 2500, straight = 1500, six of a kind = 3000, three pairs = 1500, 4+pair = 1500 — ported verbatim so outcomes stay checkable against the source engine. 11 Single 1 = 100, single 5 = 50, no other single scores. 12 Multiplier applies to the whole hand and is the only place a modifier enters.

BOARD AND CASCADE (13-22)
13 Cleared cells empty and the column above falls, standard match-3 gravity. 14 Refill from the draw-ordinal stream, so the forecast strip works unchanged. 15 Gravity is a pure function of the board, so replay reproduces it. 16 A cascade that itself scores is NOT auto-banked — the player must still choose. 17 Reshuffle when no scoring chain exists anywhere on the board, detected not guessed. 18 The no-chain detector must be exhaustive over connected paths of length <= 6, memoised. 19 Board stagnation concedes after bounded attempts rather than looping. 20 Chain preview: as the player drags, the running hand score is shown live. 21 The preview uses the SAME lookupScore the executor will use, so a client can never show a number the server disagrees with. 22 Illegal extensions of a chain are greyed, not silently ignored.

BOMBS AND SPECIALS (23-30)
23 triggersBomb already returns BOMB_STANDARD on six-of-a-kind and BOMB_RAINBOW on a straight — wire those rather than inventing new triggers. 24 BOMB_STANDARD clears the 3x3 around the chain's last cell. 25 BOMB_RAINBOW clears every cell of one face value. 26 Bombs are earned by a named combo, never by a random drop, so the player can aim for them. 27 The bomb is shown in the forecast strip when the chain that would trigger it is available. 28 No purchasable specials. 29 No timed specials. 30 Wildcards are FALLIBLE claims — a wildcard's displayed face is the engine's guess until the chain closes, which is the project's contested-state discipline.

MODES (31-38)
31 SOLO: fixed turns, score is the bank. 32 VS: shared seed, identical boards, blind settlement — neither player sees the other's total until both close, because in async play the second mover would otherwise know the target. 33 COOP: two players, ONE board, alternating turns, a shared bank, and a shared farkle. 34 Coop's real mechanic: a farkle by either player costs the SHARED unbanked pot, so the decision to push is a negotiation. 35 Coop is not two solo games summed — that would be a leaderboard, not cooperation. 36 All three modes run the same executor. 37 Mode is a config field, never a second rules path. 38 VS settles pari-mutuel on rank, so the scoring scale cannot affect who wins.

FORECAST AND IR/UV (39-45)
39 Row 1 of the strip shows the next six faces entering the board — certain, from the draw ordinal. 40 Row 2 shows the six after — fallible, because a cascade changes how many cells refill. 41 That fallibility is REAL here in a way it is not in lattice: cascade depth is not knowable before the chain resolves. 42 Confidence = how many cells will certainly clear, quantised to four states. 43 The forecast is a UV-3 synthetic claim and is marked as such by geometry, not colour. 44 An IR halo BENEATH a tile marks cells that a currently-available chain would clear — forecast under fact, per the band-law. 45 The halo never brightens the tile and never spills into the gutter.

VISUAL IDENTITY (46-52)
46 Farkle's identity is THE PIP. Tokens are dice, drawn through the existing 4D projection, and the game reads as dice from across the room. 47 Its palette axis is AMBER — warm, the colour of a table felt lamp — against the shared dark ground. 48 Chemistry keeps CYAN, darkmatter takes MAGENTA, so the three are distinguishable in a launcher at thumbnail size. 49 The chain is drawn as a physical ribbon threading the dice, not as selection outlines. 50 A scoring combo names itself on screen — 'Two Triplets', not '2500' — because signature recognition measured better than value comparison in the source I have. 51 The bank action is the loudest thing on the screen, since it is the only irreversible one. 52 Farkle is announced by the board going still, not by a red flash.

─────────── WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING ───────────

Nothing is measured. The Monte Carlo run for this game has not been written. I do not know whether chain-tracing has a dominant degenerate strategy, and idea 5 is my guess at why it might not.

questions.text: The core join is: trace a connected path of up to six cells, score the faces under it as a Farkle hand. Is that a real game, or does the adjacency constraint and the hand-scoring constraint fight each other in a way that makes most boards trivially solvable or trivially dead?
Idea 34 makes a coop farkle cost the shared unbanked pot. Does that produce cooperation, or does it produce one player refusing to ever push and the other resenting it?
Ideas 9 and 50 publish the pay table and name the combo. Does making the scoring fully transparent raise the skill ceiling, or does it just reveal that the optimal policy is a lookup?
Which of the 52 is most likely to be unimplementable as stated once it meets a 6x6 grid and a six-cell path — name the specific mechanical conflict.
What is the dominant degenerate strategy you would expect a solver to find in this design, and what measurement would detect it?
